claim: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide.
source: Despite current advancements in research and therapeutics, lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide.
evidence: This is a statement presented in the abstract without specific data or citation in this sentence, but represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Resistance to chemotherapeutic agents is the main reason lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality.
source: This is mainly due to the resistance that patients develop against chemotherapeutic agents over the course of treatment.
evidence: This is stated as a causal explanation in the abstract.

claim: Augmented levels of AXL and GAS6 drive resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors in certain NSCLC tumors with mesenchymal-like features.
source: In the context of non-small cell lung cancers (NSCLC) harboring EGFR-oncogenic mutations, augmented levels of AXL and GAS6 have been found to drive resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as Erlotinib and Osimertinib in certain tumors with mesenchymal-like features.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction section (Zhang et al., 2012; Byers et al., 2013; Walter et al., 2013; Elkabets et al., 2015).

claim: AXL-positive cells are already present as a subpopulation in Erlotinib-naïve tumors and tumor-derived cell lines.
source: We demonstrate that AXL-positive cells are already present as a subpopulation of cancer cells in Erlotinib-naïve tumors and tumor-derived cell lines and that the expression of AXL is regulated through a stochastic mechanism centered on the epigenetic regulation of miR-335.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: The expression of AXL is regulated through a stochastic mechanism centered on the epigenetic regulation of miR-335.
source: We demonstrate that AXL-positive cells are already present as a subpopulation of cancer cells in Erlotinib-naïve tumors and tumor-derived cell lines and that the expression of AXL is regulated through a stochastic mechanism centered on the epigenetic regulation of miR-335.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figures 3-6.

claim: More than a million patients worldwide are diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer each year.
source: Each year, more than a million patients worldwide are diagnosed with non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (Brose et al., 2002; Samuels et al., 2004; Stephens et al., 2004; Haber et al., 2005; Bean et al., 2007; Pillai and Ramalingam, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: EGFR-oncogenic mutations are present in 15-30% of NSCLC patients.
source: In 2014, the discovery that EGFR-oncogenic mutations were present in 15–30% of NSCLC patients and that the vast majority of patients harboring such mutations are particularly sensitive to treatment with EGFR inhibitors (TKi) such as Erlotinib and Gefitinib was a critical breakthrough (Lynch et al., 2004; Paez et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lynch et al., 2004 and Paez et al., 2004.

claim: The vast majority of NSCLC patients harboring EGFR-oncogenic mutations are particularly sensitive to treatment with EGFR inhibitors such as Erlotinib and Gefitinib.
source: In 2014, the discovery that EGFR-oncogenic mutations were present in 15–30% of NSCLC patients and that the vast majority of patients harboring such mutations are particularly sensitive to treatment with EGFR inhibitors (TKi) such as Erlotinib and Gefitinib was a critical breakthrough (Lynch et al., 2004; Paez et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lynch et al., 2004 and Paez et al., 2004.

claim: Within a year of treatment with EGFR TKIs, almost all patients experience relapse.
source: Yet, the success of this biomarker-based targeted therapy has been hampered by the occurrence of drug resistance. In fact, within a year of treatment with EGFR TKIs, almost all patients experience relapse (Bell et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bell et al., 2005.

claim: Secondary/gatekeeper mutations in EGFR (T790M) are molecular determinants of EGFR TKi resistance.
source: Using both experimental systems and patient samples, secondary/gatekeeper mutations in EGFR (T790M), c-Met amplifications, PI3K mutations, and the acquisition of mesenchymal and small-cell lung cancer features have been identified and validated as molecular determinants of EGFR TKi resistance (Bell et al., 2005; Engelman et al., 2006; Shaw et al., 2009; Yao et al., 2010; Shaw and Engelman, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: c-Met amplifications are molecular determinants of EGFR TKi resistance.
source: Using both experimental systems and patient samples, secondary/gatekeeper mutations in EGFR (T790M), c-Met amplifications, PI3K mutations, and the acquisition of mesenchymal and small-cell lung cancer features have been identified and validated as molecular determinants of EGFR TKi resistance (Bell et al., 2005; Engelman et al., 2006; Shaw et al., 2009; Yao et al., 2010; Shaw and Engelman, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: PI3K mutations are molecular determinants of EGFR TKi resistance.
source: Using both experimental systems and patient samples, secondary/gatekeeper mutations in EGFR (T790M), c-Met amplifications, PI3K mutations, and the acquisition of mesenchymal and small-cell lung cancer features have been identified and validated as molecular determinants of EGFR TKi resistance (Bell et al., 2005; Engelman et al., 2006; Shaw et al., 2009; Yao et al., 2010; Shaw and Engelman, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The acquisition of mesenchymal features is a molecular determinant of EGFR TKi resistance.
source: Using both experimental systems and patient samples, secondary/gatekeeper mutations in EGFR (T790M), c-Met amplifications, PI3K mutations, and the acquisition of mesenchymal and small-cell lung cancer features have been identified and validated as molecular determinants of EGFR TKi resistance (Bell et al., 2005; Engelman et al., 2006; Shaw et al., 2009; Yao et al., 2010; Shaw and Engelman, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The expression of AXL is an additional mechanism of acquired resistance in EGFR TKi-resistant tumors with mesenchymal-like features.
source: More recently, the expression of AXL has also been reported as an additional mechanism of acquired resistance in EGFR TKi-resistant tumors with mesenchymal-like features (Zhang et al., 2012; Byers et al., 2013; Walter et al., 2013; Elkabets et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: AXL is a member of the TAM (Tyro-AXL-Mer) receptor tyrosine kinase family.
source: AXL is a member of the TAM (Tyro-AXL-Mer) receptor tyrosine kinase family.
evidence: This is established knowledge about AXL.

claim: TAM receptors regulate a variety of cellular responses including cell survival, proliferation, motility, and differentiation.
source: These receptors regulate a variety of cellular responses including cell survival, proliferation, motility, as well as differentiation (Zhang et al., 2008; Ghosh et al., 2011; Ben-Batalla et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: AXL is expressed in many embryonic tissues and participates in mesenchymal and neuronal development.
source: AXL is expressed in many embryonic tissues and participates in mesenchymal and neuronal development.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: In adult tissue, AXL expression is usually restricted to smooth muscle cells.
source: In adult tissue, its expression is usually restricted to smooth muscle cells, but it has been observed to be overexpressed in several human tumors of different tissue origins (Zhang et al., 2008; Ghosh et al., 2011; Ben-Batalla et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: AXL has been observed to be overexpressed in several human tumors of different tissue origins.
source: In adult tissue, its expression is usually restricted to smooth muscle cells, but it has been observed to be overexpressed in several human tumors of different tissue origins (Zhang et al., 2008; Ghosh et al., 2011; Ben-Batalla et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: AXL possesses an extracellular domain with two N-terminal immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domains and two fibronectin type III (FNIII) repeats that bind to the GAS6 ligand.
source: AXL possesses an extracellular domain with two N-terminal immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domains and two fibronectin type III (FNIII) repeats that bind to the growth-arrest-specific 6 (GAS6) ligand (O'Bryan et al., 1991; Mark et al., 1996; Nagata et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: The binding of AXL to GAS6 enables the trans-auto-phosphorylation of AXL's intracellular tyrosine kinase domain.
source: The binding of AXL to GAS6 – upon its paracrine or autocrine secretion – enables the trans-auto-phosphorylation of AXL's intracellular tyrosine kinase domain and, consequently, the activation of multiple downstream signaling cascades (Braunger et al., 1997; Prasad et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Higher levels of AXL and GAS6 have been observed in tumors that developed resistance to Erlotinib and Osimertinib.
source: In the context of NSCLC, higher levels of AXL and GAS6 have been observed in tumors that developed resistance to Erlotinib and Osimertinib (Zhang et al., 2012; Byers et al., 2013; Taniguchi et al., 2019; Chen and Riess, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Targeting AXL by chemical or genetic inhibition restored Erlotinib sensitivity in resistant tumors.
source: In these tumors, targeting AXL by either chemical or genetic inhibition restored Erlotinib sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior research.

claim: Forced expression of an active AXL kinase in Erlotinib-sensitive tumor cells was sufficient to induce Erlotinib resistance.
source: Alternatively, forced expression of an active AXL kinase in Erlotinib-sensitive tumor cells was sufficient to induce Erlotinib resistance (Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2012.

claim: No mutations or amplifications of the AXL locus have been described in AXL-positive/Erlotinib-resistant cells.
source: Unlike other receptor tyrosine kinases, no mutations or amplifications of the AXL locus have been described in AXL-positive/Erlotinib-resistant cells (Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wu et al., 2014.

claim: The transition between AXL-positive and AXL-negative cells is highly plastic.
source: Consistent with this model, we found that the transition between AXL-positive and AXL-negative cells is highly plastic.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: The generation of AXL-positive cells is not generated via genetic mutations.
source: The generation of AXL-positive cells is neither generated via genetic mutations nor dependent on the micro-environment or drug treatment (Bell et al., 2005; Engelman et al., 2006; Shaw et al., 2009; Yao et al., 2010; Shaw and Engelman, 2016).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: The generation of AXL-positive cells is not dependent on the micro-environment.
source: The generation of AXL-positive cells is neither generated via genetic mutations nor dependent on the micro-environment or drug treatment (Bell et al., 2005; Engelman et al., 2006; Shaw et al., 2009; Yao et al., 2010; Shaw and Engelman, 2016).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: The generation of AXL-positive cells is not dependent on drug treatment.
source: The generation of AXL-positive cells is neither generated via genetic mutations nor dependent on the micro-environment or drug treatment (Bell et al., 2005; Engelman et al., 2006; Shaw et al., 2009; Yao et al., 2010; Shaw and Engelman, 2016).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: AXL-positive cells are actively dividing, unlike quiescent AKT1low cancer cells.
source: Also different from quiescent AKT1low cancer cells described by the Ramaswamy group, AXL-positive cells are actively dividing (Kabraji et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a distinguishing feature with citation to Kabraji et al., 2017.

claim: The generation of AXL-positive cells is centered on the methylation of a specific CpG island present in the promoter of MEST.
source: At the molecular level, we showed that the generation of AXL-positive cells is centered on the methylation of a specific CpG island present in the promoter of MEST, a gene that contains the miRNA miR-335 in its second intron.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: MEST contains the miRNA miR-335 in its second intron.
source: At the molecular level, we showed that the generation of AXL-positive cells is centered on the methylation of a specific CpG island present in the promoter of MEST, a gene that contains the miRNA miR-335 in its second intron.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the genomic organization.

claim: Forced down-regulation of miR-335 in AXL-negative cells was sufficient to increase the expression of AXL.
source: In particular, we showed that forced down-regulation of miR-335 in AXL-negative cells was sufficient to increase the expression of AXL and to induce phenotypic and molecular features that are characteristic of AXL-positive cells, such as epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and Erlotinib resistance.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Forced down-regulation of miR-335 in AXL-negative cells was sufficient to induce epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition.
source: In particular, we showed that forced down-regulation of miR-335 in AXL-negative cells was sufficient to increase the expression of AXL and to induce phenotypic and molecular features that are characteristic of AXL-positive cells, such as epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and Erlotinib resistance.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Forced down-regulation of miR-335 in AXL-negative cells was sufficient to induce Erlotinib resistance.
source: In particular, we showed that forced down-regulation of miR-335 in AXL-negative cells was sufficient to increase the expression of AXL and to induce phenotypic and molecular features that are characteristic of AXL-positive cells, such as epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and Erlotinib resistance.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: H1650-M3 and PC14 cells harbor EGFR-oncogenic mutations.
source: These cells are derivative of H1650 and PC9 cells, respectively, harbor EGFR -oncogenic mutations, and were previously generated by culturing the parental cells with constant high concentrations of Erlotinib (Yao et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the cell lines used in the study.

claim: H1650-M3 and PC14 cells were generated by culturing parental cells with constant high concentrations of Erlotinib.
source: These cells are derivative of H1650 and PC9 cells, respectively, harbor EGFR -oncogenic mutations, and were previously generated by culturing the parental cells with constant high concentrations of Erlotinib (Yao et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Yao et al., 2010.

claim: AXL-positive cells are present in multiple Erlotinib-naïve cell populations.
source: By using the AXL-positive cell lines, H1650-M3 and PC14 as reference (Figure 1A,B), we observed the presence of AXL-positive cells in multiple Erlotinib-naïve cell populations (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by FACS data shown in Figure 1B-D.

claim: AXL-positive cells are present in cell lines driven by mutant KRAS (A549).
source: The presence of these AXL-positive cells was not restricted to tumor-derived cell lines harboring EGFR-oncogenic mutations, as we observed that a similar percentage of AXL-positive cells were present also in cell lines driven for example by mutant KRAS (i.e., A549) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is a finding supported by data in Figure 1C,D.

claim: GAS6 is expressed at high levels in FACS-sorted AXL-positive cells.
source: Our RT-PCR and western blot analysis confirmed the high expression of AXL and GAS6 in these cells (Figure 1D–F) and indicated that AXL, as well as AKT, were constitutively phosphorylated in AXL-positive cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR and western blot data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: AXL is constitutively phosphorylated in AXL-positive cells.
source: Our RT-PCR and western blot analysis confirmed the high expression of AXL and GAS6 in these cells (Figure 1D–F) and indicated that AXL, as well as AKT, were constitutively phosphorylated in AXL-positive cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: AKT is constitutively phosphorylated in AXL-positive cells.
source: Our RT-PCR and western blot analysis confirmed the high expression of AXL and GAS6 in these cells (Figure 1D–F) and indicated that AXL, as well as AKT, were constitutively phosphorylated in AXL-positive cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Human primary drug-naïve NSCLC tumors contain a subpopulation of cells with high expression of AXL and GAS6.
source: Also in this case, we found that human primary drug-naïve tumors contained a subpopulation of cells with high expression of AXL and GAS6 (Figure 1G,H, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data from five primary NSCLC tumors shown in Figure 1G,H.

claim: AXL-positive FACS-sorted cells from Erlotinib-naïve cell lines have similar sensitivity to Erlotinib treatment as AXL-positive cells generated upon Erlotinib selection.
source: We found that AXL-positive FACS-sorted cells from Erlotinib-naïve cell lines (i.e., PC9 AXL+ve) and AXL-positive cells that were generated upon Erlotinib selection (i.e., PC14) had similar sensitivity to Erlotinib treatment with IC50 almost three times higher than parental cells (i.e., PC9) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by drug sensitivity assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Pre-existing AXL-positive cells have an IC50 for Erlotinib almost three times higher than parental AXL-negative cells.
source: We found that AXL-positive FACS-sorted cells from Erlotinib-naïve cell lines (i.e., PC9 AXL+ve) and AXL-positive cells that were generated upon Erlotinib selection (i.e., PC14) had similar sensitivity to Erlotinib treatment with IC50 almost three times higher than parental cells (i.e., PC9) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by drug sensitivity assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Pre-existing AXL+ cells can be the main source of Erlotinib resistance.
source: Because this study was conducted in a short period (96 hr after sorting), our data further solidify our conclusion that pre-existing AXL+ cells can be the main source of Erlotinib resistance.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on lineage tracing experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: AXL-positive cells are characterized by mesenchymal features such as an increase in stress fibers.
source: Morphologically, the FACS-sorted AXL+ cells looked very similar to the AXL+ cells that emerged following Erlotinib treatment (PC14 and H1650-M3). All possessed the morphological and molecular features of mesenchymal cells, including loss of cobblestone shape and increased stress fibers (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2C) and differential expression of mesenchymal and epithelial markers (e.g., TGF-β1, TGF-β2, Slug, Twist, Vimentin, and Zeb1) (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2D; Zhang et al., 2012; Byers et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: AXL-positive cells have differential expression of mesenchymal markers including TGF-β1, TGF-β2, Slug, Twist, Vimentin, and Zeb1.
source: All possessed the morphological and molecular features of mesenchymal cells, including loss of cobblestone shape and increased stress fibers (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2C) and differential expression of mesenchymal and epithelial markers (e.g., TGF-β1, TGF-β2, Slug, Twist, Vimentin, and Zeb1) (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2D; Zhang et al., 2012; Byers et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The mesenchymal phenotypic features of AXL-positive cells are driven by AXL.
source: These phenotypic features were driven by AXL because the inactivation of AXL in AXL-positive cells using the pharmacological inhibitor BMS-777607 resulted in the loss of the mesenchymal marker Vimentin and increased expression of E-cadherin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by pharmacological inhibition experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Inactivation of AXL in AXL-positive cells results in the loss of the mesenchymal marker Vimentin.
source: These phenotypic features were driven by AXL because the inactivation of AXL in AXL-positive cells using the pharmacological inhibitor BMS-777607 resulted in the loss of the mesenchymal marker Vimentin and increased expression of E-cadherin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Inactivation of AXL in AXL-positive cells results in increased expression of E-cadherin.
source: These phenotypic features were driven by AXL because the inactivation of AXL in AXL-positive cells using the pharmacological inhibitor BMS-777607 resulted in the loss of the mesenchymal marker Vimentin and increased expression of E-cadherin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: AXL-positive cells are represented at a very low percentage in H1703, H1975, and H23 mesenchymal cell lines.
source: Despite H1703, H1975, and H23 cells present with clear mesenchymal characteristics, AXL-positive cells were represented at a very low percentage in these cell lines and virtually absent in the H1703 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: This is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claim: AXL-positive cells are a unique cell population with features that only partially overlap with other mesenchymal cells.
source: Hence we concluded that while all mesenchymal cells share common characteristics such as increased stress fibers, increased motility, elongated shape, etc.; AXL-positive cells are a unique cell population with features that only partially overlap with other mesenchymal cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that not all mesenchymal cells are AXL-positive.

claim: The percentages of AXL-positive cells are similar in multiple clonal cell lines derived from a single AXL-negative cell.
source: We observed a very similar percentage of AXL-positive cells in the parental cells as well as in the single-cell derived clonal cell lines (Figure 3C,D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: AXL-positive cells are most likely generated from AXL-negative cells via a non-genetic, stochastic mechanism.
source: Based on this finding, we concluded that AXL-positive cells are most likely generated from AXL-negative cells via a non-genetic, stochastic mechanism.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the clonal analysis data in Figure 3.

claim: Within 3 weeks, AXL-negative cells can regenerate cell populations with the same percentage of AXL-positive and AXL-negative cells as the parental cell line.
source: We found that within 3 weeks, the AXL-negative cells could regenerate cell populations with the same percentage of AXL-positive and AXL-negative cells as the parental cell line.
evidence: This is supported by longitudinal FACS data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: AXL-positive cells can regenerate a progeny population with the same percentages of AXL-positive and AXL-negative cells as present in the parental cell line, but it takes 18 weeks.
source: Interestingly, we observed that even though the AXL-positive cells took a longer time to do so (18 weeks), they too were able to regenerate a progeny population with the same percentages of AXL-positive and AXL-negative cells as present in the parental cell line.
evidence: This is supported by longitudinal FACS data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: 20 miRNAs were upregulated in AXL-positive H1650-M3 cells compared to AXL-negative H1650 cells.
source: Using these criteria, we identified 20 miRNAs that were upregulated and 19 miRNAs that were downregulated in the AXL-positive H1650-M3 cells compared to the AXL-negative H1650 cells (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is based on deep sequencing data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 19 miRNAs were downregulated in AXL-positive H1650-M3 cells compared to AXL-negative H1650 cells.
source: Using these criteria, we identified 20 miRNAs that were upregulated and 19 miRNAs that were downregulated in the AXL-positive H1650-M3 cells compared to the AXL-negative H1650 cells (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is based on deep sequencing data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: miR-335 suppresses a mesenchymal-like state and metastatic dissemination.
source: It has been reported that miR-335 suppresses a mesenchymal-like state and metastatic dissemination by targeting a diverse set of genes regulating cell migration, extracellular matrix remodeling, cell self-renewal, and epigenetic reprogramming (Tavazoie et al., 2008; Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tavazoie et al., 2008.

claim: miR-335 targets genes regulating cell migration, extracellular matrix remodeling, cell self-renewal, and epigenetic reprogramming.
source: It has been reported that miR-335 suppresses a mesenchymal-like state and metastatic dissemination by targeting a diverse set of genes regulating cell migration, extracellular matrix remodeling, cell self-renewal, and epigenetic reprogramming (Tavazoie et al., 2008; Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tavazoie et al., 2008.

claim: TGF-β is a well-known regulator of AXL and AXL activity.
source: In fact, TGF-β is a well-known regulator of AXL and AXL activity (Lynch et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lynch et al., 2012.

claim: The TGF-β axis suppresses the expression of multiple miRNAs that are downregulated in AXL-positive cells.
source: Furthermore, the TGF-β axis has also been shown to suppress the expression of multiple miRNAs that we found to be downregulated in AXL-positive cells (Gregory et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2012; Kato et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gregory et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2012; Kato et al., 2013.

claim: miR-335 levels are decreased in all AXL-positive cells examined.
source: In all these cases, when we measured the expression of miR-335 by qRT-PCR, we consistently found that miR-335 levels were decreased in all AXL-positive cells (Figure 4E–G).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4E-G.

claim: miR-335 targets SOX4, TNC, COL1A1, PTPRN2, MERTK, PLCB1, LAMB2, FGF2, JAG1, BMI1, SMARCA2, and MAX are expressed at higher levels in AXL-positive cells.
source: RT-PCR analysis showed that the miR-335 targets SOX4, TNC, COL1A1, PTPRN2, MERTK, PLCB1, LAMB2, FGF2, JAG1, BMI1, SMARCA2, and MAX were expressed at higher levels in AXL-positive cells; miR-335 low cells (H1650-M3) compared to AXL-negative cells; and miR-335 high cells (H1650) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Antagomir treatment decreased the expression of miR-335.
source: We found that the Antagomirs treatment decreased the expression of miR-335 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and of its targets (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) as well as of TGF-β 1/2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C) and of the TGF-β target genes VIM, Ecadh, SNAI, SLUG, etc. compared to control (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Antagomir treatment decreased the expression of miR-335 targets.
source: We found that the Antagomirs treatment decreased the expression of miR-335 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and of its targets (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) as well as of TGF-β 1/2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C) and of the TGF-β target genes VIM, Ecadh, SNAI, SLUG, etc. compared to control (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Antagomir treatment decreased the expression of TGF-β 1/2.
source: We found that the Antagomirs treatment decreased the expression of miR-335 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and of its targets (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) as well as of TGF-β 1/2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C) and of the TGF-β target genes VIM, Ecadh, SNAI, SLUG, etc. compared to control (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Treatment of AXL-negative cell lines with miR-335 Antagomir resulted in increased expression of AXL-positive cells.
source: We observed that treatment of AXL-negative cell lines (H1650 and PC9) with a miR-335 Antagomir resulted in a reduction of miR-335 expression (Figure 5A) and an increased expression of AXL-positive cells (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Treatment with miR-335 Antagomir increased the resistance of cells to Erlotinib treatment.
source: In a standard drug sensitivity assay, we observed that treatment with miR-335 Antagomir also increased the resistance of cells to Erlotinib treatment to levels similar to what we observed when we tested the AXL-positive cell lines we derived by Erlotinib selection (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: This is supported by drug sensitivity assay data shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: Genetic inactivation of miR-335 using CRISPR-CAS9 resulted in the acquisition of phenotypic and molecular characteristics of AXL-positive cells.
source: Also in this case and consistent with our previous results, genetic inactivation of miR-335 resulted in the acquisition of phenotypic and molecular characteristics of AXL-positive cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Expression of miR-335 mimic oligonucleotides in AXL+ cells resulted in a dramatic decrease in cell viability.
source: Interestingly, when we express miR-335 mimic oligonucleotides in the AXL+ cells H1650-M3 and PC14, we observed a dramatic decrease in cell viability (Figure 5G–H).
evidence: This is supported by crystal violet staining data shown in Figure 5G-H.

claim: The transition of cells into AXL+ cell state induced the rewiring of cell signalings to which cells become 'addicted'.
source: Hence, the transition of cells into AXL+ cell state induced the rewiring of cell signalings to which cells become 'addicted'.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that miR-335 expression is lethal to AXL+ cells.

claim: miR-335 serves as a critical regulator of the interconversion of AXL-negative and AXL-positive cell states.
source: Altogether, these observations indicate that miR-335 serves as a critical regulator of the interconversion of AXL-negative and AXL-positive cell states beyond its well-studied role in the regulation of metastasis (Tavazoie et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: The miR-335 encoding sequence resides in the second intron of the MEST/PEG1 gene located on chromosome 7q32.
source: The miR-335 encoding sequence resides in the second intron of the mesoderm-specific transcript homolog (MEST)/paternally expressed 1 (PEG1) gene located on chromosome 7q32.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about genomic organization.

claim: Two distinct CpG islands have been identified in the promoters of MEST in humans.
source: In humans, two distinct CpG islands have been identified in the promoters of MEST (Figure 6A; Png et al., 2011; Dohi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Png et al., 2011 and Dohi et al., 2013.

claim: CpG island 1 of MEST is differentially methylated in AXL-positive H1650-M3 cells.
source: We found that although no significant differences were observed in the methylation of CpG island 2, CpG island 1 was differentially methylated in the AXL-positive H1650-M3 cells and associated with higher expression of MEST isoform 1 and decreased expression of miR-335 (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by bisulfite sequencing and methylation-specific PCR data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Differential methylation of CpG island 1 is associated with higher expression of MEST isoform 1 and decreased expression of miR-335.
source: We found that although no significant differences were observed in the methylation of CpG island 2, CpG island 1 was differentially methylated in the AXL-positive H1650-M3 cells and associated with higher expression of MEST isoform 1 and decreased expression of miR-335 (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: All AXL-positive cells from FACS-sorted cell lines and human NSCLC tumor-derived cells displayed increased methylation of CpG island 1 relative to AXL-negative cells.
source: Again, we found that all AXL-positive cells displayed increased methylation of CpG island 1 relative to AXL-negative cells (Figure 6C,D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by methylation-specific PCR data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: Treatment with 5-Aza-dC results in a dose-dependent change in the methylation of CpG island 1.
source: We observed a dose-dependent change in the methylation of CpG island 1 and, consistent with the role of CpG island hypermethylation in gene silencing, increased expression of miR-335 in AXL-positive cells (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is supported by methylation-specific PCR data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Treatment with 5-Aza-dC results in increased expression of miR-335 in AXL-positive cells.
source: We observed a dose-dependent change in the methylation of CpG island 1 and, consistent with the role of CpG island hypermethylation in gene silencing, increased expression of miR-335 in AXL-positive cells (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Inhibition of miR-335 by Antagomir treatment impeded the decrease in the number of AXL-positive cells in H1650-M3 cells treated by 5-Aza-dC.
source: These changes were most likely due to increased miR-335 levels as inhibition of miR-335 by Antagomir treatment impeded the observed decrease in the number of AXL-positive cells in H1650-M3 cells (AXL-positive) treated by 5-Aza-dC (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Treatment with 5-Aza-dC increased sensitivity of H1650 cells to Erlotinib.
source: Consistent with 5-Aza-dC decreasing MEST promoter methylation and the viability of AXL-positive cells (Figure 6E–G), we observed a decrease in AXL-positive cells in H1650 cells upon 5-Aza-dC treatment (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D) and overall increased sensitivity of H1650 cells to Erlotinib (Figure 6H).
evidence: This is supported by drug sensitivity assay data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Differential miR-335 promoter methylation is responsible for the decreased expression of miR-335 observed in AXL-positive cells.
source: Based on these observations, we concluded that differential miR-335 promoter methylation is responsible for the decreased expression of miR-335 observed in AXL-positive cells and that the transition between the AXL-positive and AXL-negative cell states as well as their differential resistance to EGFR TKi is regulated epigenetically.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the methylation and functional studies.

claim: The transition between the AXL-positive and AXL-negative cell states is regulated epigenetically.
source: Based on these observations, we concluded that differential miR-335 promoter methylation is responsible for the decreased expression of miR-335 observed in AXL-positive cells and that the transition between the AXL-positive and AXL-negative cell states as well as their differential resistance to EGFR TKi is regulated epigenetically.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the methylation and functional studies.

claim: Approximately 15% of tumors that become resistant to EGFR TKi are characterized by mesenchymal-like features and higher expression of AXL.
source: In the case of lung tumors driven by oncogenic-EFGR mutations, it has been observed that approximately 15% of tumors that become resistant to EGFR TKi are characterized by mesenchymal-like features and higher expression of AXL.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the literature.

claim: In tumors with mesenchymal-like features and higher AXL expression, inhibition of AXL restores sensitivity to EGFR TKi.
source: In these tumors inhibition of AXL restore the sensitivity to EGFR TKi (Zhang et al., 2012; Taniguchi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2012 and Taniguchi et al., 2019.

claim: AXL was neither mutated nor amplified in AXL-positive EGFR TKi-resistant tumor cells.
source: In contrast to other mechanisms of resistance to EGFR TKi, in these tumor cells, AXL was neither mutated, amplified, nor its expression driven by EGFR TKi treatment as in the case of the persistent cells originally described by Sharma et al., 2010.
evidence: This is stated as a distinguishing feature with citation to Sharma et al., 2010.

claim: The expression of AXL in resistant cells is not driven by EGFR TKi treatment.
source: In contrast to other mechanisms of resistance to EGFR TKi, in these tumor cells, AXL was neither mutated, amplified, nor its expression driven by EGFR TKi treatment as in the case of the persistent cells originally described by Sharma et al., 2010.
evidence: This is stated as a distinguishing feature with citation to Sharma et al., 2010.

claim: The switch between AXL-negative and AXL-positive cell states is restricted by miR-335.
source: The switch between these two cell states is restricted by miR-335 as all AXL-positive cells we examined were characterized by a decreased expression of miR-335 and that inactivation of miR-335 decreased the number of AXL-positive cells and reverted AXL-positive cells into AXL-negative cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: AXL mRNA does not contain a miR-335 seeding sequence.
source: Although miR-335 restricts the transition of AXL-positive into AXL-negative cells, AXL mRNA does not contain a miR-335 seeding sequence, which means it is unlikely to be a direct target of miR-335.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about the sequence.

claim: AXL is unlikely to be a direct target of miR-335.
source: Although miR-335 restricts the transition of AXL-positive into AXL-negative cells, AXL mRNA does not contain a miR-335 seeding sequence, which means it is unlikely to be a direct target of miR-335.
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of a miR-335 seeding sequence in AXL mRNA.

claim: miR-335 regulates the expression of components of the TGF-β axis.
source: Yet, miR-335 has been previously shown to regulate the expression of a multitude of signaling pathways including components of the TGF-β axis.
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge from the literature.

claim: AXL is a known downstream target of TGF-β.
source: The regulation of the TGF-β axis by miR-335 is of particular interest because AXL is a known downstream target of TGF-β, hence suggesting a possible molecular linking AXL and miR-335 (Bauer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bauer et al., 2012.

claim: Exposure to TGF-β regulates the expression of several miRNAs associated with the AXL-positive state.
source: The inhibition of the TGF-β signaling pathway by miR-335 is particularly interesting also because exposure to TGF-β regulate the expression of several of the miRNAs associated with the AXL-positive state, such as miR-20a, miR-34a, miR-200c, etc.
evidence: This is stated as an observation connecting TGF-β to miRNA regulation.

claim: The mir-200 family members induce EMT and resistance to Erlotinib.
source: Among them of particular significance were the mir-200 family members, as they not only induce EMT but also resistance to Erlotinib (Brabletz and Brabletz, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Brabletz and Brabletz, 2010.

claim: miR-335 is among approximately 50 miRNAs that are regulated epigenetically by DNA methylation of CpG islands within promoter regions.
source: Lastly, miR-335 is among approximately 50 miRNAs that are regulated epigenetically by DNA methylation of CpG islands within promoter regions (Lujambio and Esteller, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lujambio and Esteller, 2007.

claim: It takes AXL-negative cells a few weeks to generate a population with the same distribution of AXL-positive and AXL-negative cells as the parental cell line.
source: While within a few weeks the AXL-negative cells generated a population of cells with the same distribution of AXL-positive and AXL-negative cells as was observed in the parental cell line; it took the AXL-positive cells a couple of months to reach this equilibrium.
evidence: This is based on the longitudinal FACS data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: It takes AXL-positive cells a couple of months to generate a population with the same distribution of AXL-positive and AXL-negative cells as the parental cell line.
source: While within a few weeks the AXL-negative cells generated a population of cells with the same distribution of AXL-positive and AXL-negative cells as was observed in the parental cell line; it took the AXL-positive cells a couple of months to reach this equilibrium.
evidence: This is based on the longitudinal FACS data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: AXL-positive cells grow slower than AXL-negative cells.
source: At this time, we do not have a clear molecular mechanism explaining these differences, yet it is tentative to hypothesize that – given the stochastic regulation of miR335 – because the AXL-positive cells grow slower than AXL-negative cells, it will take a longer time for the former to switch state.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis to explain the differential kinetics of cell state transitions.

claim: The de-methylation rate of CpG1 on the miR-335 promoter could occur less efficiently than its methylation.
source: Alternatively, it is tempting to postulate that the interconversion between the two cell states could be regulated by enzymatic activities occurring at different rates. This hypothesis is informed by the possibility that the de-methylation rate of the CpG1 on the miR-335 promoter could occur less efficiently than its methylation.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative hypothesis.

claim: AXL-negative cells could emerge over time following drug removal in AXL-positive tumors.
source: Consequently, as shown in the schematic in Figure 7, AXL-negative cells could hypothetically emerge over time following drug removal.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the plasticity of cell states.

claim: Certain Erlotinib-resistant tumors expressing neuroendocrine markers can revert to an epithelial-like state over time upon interruption of drug treatment.
source: This phenomenon is in principle similar to the observation that certain Erlotinib-resistant tumors expressing neuroendocrine markers can revert to an epithelial-like state over time upon interruption of the drug treatment (Niederst et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Niederst et al., 2015.

claim: AXL-positive cells that survived drug treatment can accumulate novel genetic mutations that can alter the innate equilibrium between AXL-positive and AXL-negative states.
source: Nevertheless, the AXL-positive cells that survived to the drug treatment can accumulate novel genetic mutations that can alter the innate equilibrium between AXL-positive and AXL-negative and, consequently, produce tumors that are stable AXL-positive state (Figure 7).
evidence: This is stated as a possibility based on the model.

claim: H1650-M3 and PC14 cells maintain features associated with the AXL-positive cell state even in the absence of drug treatment.
source: This explanation seems to be true for certain clonal populations, including the H1650-M3 and PC14 cells that were selected to grow and expand in the presence of high Erlotinib concentrations. In fact, these cell lines maintain features associated with the AXL-positive cell state even in the absence of drug treatment.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about these cell lines.

claim: TGF-beta can spur the accumulation of mutations and accelerate the clonal evolution of tumors by repressing DNA repair.
source: Interestingly, we have recently observed that TGF-beta by repressing DNA repair could spur the accumulation of mutations and accelerate the clonal evolution of tumors (Pal et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pal et al., 2017.

claim: Reactivation of miR-335 resulted in a dramatic decrease in the viability of AXL+ cells.
source: Interestingly, the reactivation of miR-335 resulted in a dramatic decrease in the viability of AXL+ cells, suggesting that the cells transiting into AXL+ cells are addicted to specific singling, regulated by miR-335.
evidence: This is based on the miR-335 mimic experiments shown in Figure 5G-H.

claim: Cells transiting into AXL+ cells are addicted to specific signaling regulated by miR-335.
source: Interestingly, the reactivation of miR-335 resulted in a dramatic decrease in the viability of AXL+ cells, suggesting that the cells transiting into AXL+ cells are addicted to specific singling, regulated by miR-335.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lethality of miR-335 expression in AXL+ cells.

claim: Treatments based only on targeting epithelial, AXL-negative cells will be insufficient and poised to fail.
source: They predict that treatments based only on targeting the epithelial, AXL-negative cells, such as in the case of Erlotinib and Osimertinib treatments, will be insufficient and poised to fail.
evidence: This is a clinical implication stated based on the findings.

claim: Combinatorial treatments targeting both cell states could increase the sensitivity of drug treatment and slow or prevent the acquisition of tumor resistance.
source: Yet, combinatorial treatments targeting both cell states could increase the sensitivity of drug treatment and slow or prevent the acquisition of tumor resistance.
evidence: This is stated as a therapeutic implication of the findings.

claim: The concentration of 5-Aza-dC to which AXL-positive cells are sensitive is within the 5-Aza-dC blood concentrations observed in clinical trials.
source: Of note, our in vitro studies indicated that the concentration of 5-Aza-dC to which AXL-positive cells are sensitive are well within the 5-Aza-dC blood concentrations observed in clinical trials for the treatment of different cancer types (Karahoca and Momparler, 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Karahoca and Momparler, 2013.
